import inspect
import structlog.typing

cls = structlog.typing.FilteringBoundLogger
sig = inspect.signature(cls.new)
actual_param = next(p.name for p in sig.parameters.values() if p.kind is inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD)
documented_param = "initial_values"  # DOC-LITERAL
assert documented_param == actual_param, f"docs say {documented_param}, signature uses {actual_param}"
print("DOCS_OK")
doc_literal_usage: FilteringBoundLogger.new documents an italicized parameter named initial_values, but inspect.signature shows the variadic keyword parameter is named new_values.
argument_finding_is_false: The mismatch is mostly cosmetic: because `new` takes `**new_values`, callers can pass `initial_values=...` and it will bind that key rather than fail. However, the docstring uses italics in the conventional parameter-position sense, so the named placeholder still conflicts with the actual variadic parameter name.
